investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to kata/peer-pod capable nodes. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 126–144 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract gap.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or a prior eval run left VM slots fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new pods at scheduling time.

Secondary — peer-pod node pool is undersized for the current eval concurrency: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and simultaneous eval runs for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime each submit a pod, potentially competing for the same limited slots.
Tertiary — a leaked or stuck remote-agent VM from a previous eval run is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up, reducing available capacity below what is needed for a new pod.

Lower confidence — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: if the selector was recently changed to target a label that no longer exists on the 2 peer-pod nodes, all 6 nodes would be ineligible; however, the scheduler message distinguishes the 2 affinity-matching nodes (resource-insufficient) from the 4 non-matching nodes, making a selector regression less likely than a capacity issue.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T22:42–22:47Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pods because 2 nodes report insufficient kata peer-pod VM capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes production cluster (6 nodes) exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector for remote agent workloads. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 126–144 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata peer-pods scheduling tier in the production-api environment. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every agent pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No agent pod reached a running state, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time; the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window (remote-agent-create at 22:42, remote-agent-state at 22:44, remote-agent-runtime at 22:44–22:47) timed out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to kata/peer-pod capable nodes. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 126–144 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract gap.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or a prior eval run left VM slots fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new pods at scheduling time.

Secondary — peer-pod node pool is undersized for the current eval concurrency: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and simultaneous eval runs for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime each submit a pod, potentially competing for the same limited slots.
Tertiary — a leaked or stuck remote-agent VM from a previous eval run is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up, reducing available capacity below what is needed for a new pod.

Lower confidence — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: if the selector was recently changed to target a label that no longer exists on the 2 peer-pod nodes, all 6 nodes would be ineligible; however, the scheduler message distinguishes the 2 affinity-matching nodes (resource-insufficient) from the 4 non-matching nodes, making a selector regression less likely than a capacity issue.

[Likely] The node affinity or selector on the eval pod restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity — a combination of resource exhaustion and topology constraint.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool from its expected size, leaving fewer slots than the eval workload requires. No node failure evidence is present in the packet, so this remains a hypothesis.

[Possible] The eval runner submitted all three remote-agent checks in rapid succession (within ~5 minutes), and concurrent pod requests from remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state consumed the remaining VM slots before remote-agent-runtime could schedule.

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in the pod's node affinity or resource request (e.g., requesting more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than available per node) could cause permanent unschedulability even on an otherwise healthy cluster.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed that the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion would be disproved and a misconfigured pod affinity or resource request would become the primary hypothesis.

If a subsequent eval run with the same probe command succeeded and produced all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), it would indicate a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the node affinity or selector on the remote agent pod was found to be misconfigured to exclude all 6 nodes (not just 4), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a scheduling misconfiguration independent of VM slot availability.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a concurrent run, it would suggest the failure is specific to the runtime probe's pod spec rather than a shared VM pool exhaustion.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause would shift to a node-level resource reporting error or a cluster configuration problem rather than slot exhaustion by running workloads.

Add a concurrent scheduling stress eval that submits two remote agent pod requests simultaneously and verifies both schedule successfully, catching capacity contention between sibling checks before it manifests in production observability runs.
